audit.summary: Confirmed major: 1 Confirmed minor: 7 Core result refuted: True
limitations: P1 — Higher-dimensional Hypothesis II admits full universal compression — Counterevidence: The phase is already correctly centered; no omitted translation normalization excludes it. Three-dimensional conclusions and analytic Propositions 5.1/5.3 under their own hypotheses are not refuted. Principal-minor restriction alone is not certified a repair because arbitrary D introduces other columns.
P2 — Kakeya non-compression index set includes the target full minor — Counterevidence: This makes the hypothesis vacuous; it is not an example satisfying I with a false conclusion.

P3 — Local inverse centred at omega=0 is not implied by H1 — Counterevidence: Subtracting the constant linear y term or centering omega at the actual gradient restores the local inverse and preserves relevant operator norms.
P4 — Wrong middle sign in Example 3.1 Jacobian — Counterevidence: The intended identically zero example has A=B=C=0, so its consequence survives.

P5 — Compact selection and inverse-polynomial assertions do not follow — Counterevidence: Taking closure within a closed bounded containing set preserves semialgebraic dimension; finite parametrizations can be selected by projected measure. Bezout can be applied in the original variables with the auxiliary constraints and nonsingular isolated roots, instead of to the inverse composition.

P6 — Local transversality does not yield M1-only multilinear uniformity — Counterevidence: Higher derivatives grow with N. This does not refute a fixed-phase estimate allowed to depend on those derivatives. Guth's actual fixed cone-axis condition is stronger than the local-X condition.

P7 — Shrinking-cap symbol derivative sign and packet centering — Counterevidence: A unit amplitude is not an example satisfying the erroneous all-order derivative hypothesis. The adjacent page supplies the intended positive derivative exponent. Physical zB must be divided by lambda inside the unit-scale phase.

P8 — Whitney separation and summation range missing in local-to-global proof — Counterevidence: A divergent proof bound is not a counterexample to the global lemma. For the required odd-dimensional application, alpha>=alpha_H is supplied by the universal theorem; below alpha_H, s alpha<s alpha_H=(n+1)/2-s(n-1)/4<=1<=(n-1)/2, giving the strict convergence range.

repair.content:
Strengthen Hypothesis II to genuine determinant/sublevel control. Directly assuming Definition 4.1 preserves only the later conditional route, subject to local corrections. Requiring principal minors alone has not been proved sufficient because arbitrary D mixes columns.

Use distinct proper-minor I_< for Kakeya and all-minor I_<= where needed for Nikodym.

Centre omega at the actual gradient or subtract its linear frequency term before shrinking the inverse-function patch.

Replace +Bt by -Bt only.

Use closure in a closed containment set, finite parametrization and projected-measure pigeonhole. Keep original polynomial parameters plus frozen-coordinate constraints for BÃ©zout.

Allow dependence on suitable higher derivative bounds and controlled fixed-cone pieces; cited Guth Theorem 7 requires fixed-axis small slopes.

Use positive derivative powers R^(|beta|/2), lambda^(|beta|/2), correct opposite modulation, and basepoint zB/lambda in unit phase.

Use non-neighbour Whitney pairs with neighbouring parents; split alpha>=alpha_H to universal estimate and apply the series only below alpha_H.
